title: A two-tap convolution
starter:
%xb = buffer 5 dtype=f32 slot=0
%wb = buffer 2 dtype=f32 slot=1
%yb = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=2
%x  = load %xb
%w  = load %wb
%y  = expand 0.0 [4]
%st = store %yb %y
%y1 = after %yb %st

hints: Every window is full here, so there is nothing to pad. You need one shifted copy of x per tap, each 4 long.
`shrink %x 0 [4]` holds `x[i]` for every i and `shrink %x 1 [4]` holds `x[i+1]`. Stack them into shape `[2 4]`.
Reshape w to `[2 1]`, expand it to `[2 4]`, multiply by the stack, and `reduce op=add pop=1` adds the two taps.

answer.code:
%xb = buffer 5 dtype=f32 slot=0
%wb = buffer 2 dtype=f32 slot=1
%yb = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=2
%x  = load %xb
%w  = load %wb
%s0 = shrink %x 0 [4]
%s1 = shrink %x 1 [4]
%win = stack %s0 %s1
%w2 = reshape %w [2 1]
%wx = expand %w2 [2 4]
%pr = mul %win %wx
%y  = reduce %pr op=add pop=1
%st = store %yb %y
%y1 = after %yb %st
answer.explain: One `shrink` per tap gives the shifted copies, `stack` puts the taps on a new leading axis, and w is expanded along the outputs. After the `mul`, a `reduce` over the tap axis leaves one sum per output. No pad is needed because no window hangs off the end.
